Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):
  • Acute upper respiratory tract illness – 1-week history of sore throat, dry cough, intermittent fever, headache, mild wheeze, chest discomfort, exertional shortness of breath; reduced appetite.  
  • No chronic medical conditions reported.  
  • No history of asthma, thromboembolic disease, hypertension, diabetes, or cardiovascular disease.

- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):
  • Mother: lung cancer.  
  • No other familial chronic diseases reported.

- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:
  • None.  
  • Paracetamol advised (dose/route/frequency not documented).

- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):
  • Not recorded.

- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:
  • Not recorded.

- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:
  • Tobacco: Non-smoker; experimented “once or twice.”  
  • Alcohol: Not recorded.  
  • Other substances: No asbestos exposure known; no illicit drug history recorded.  
  • Physical activity: Walks and “does exercises now and then.”  
  • Diet: Decreased appetite over the past week; baseline intake usually good.

- Hearing and vision concerns:
  • Not recorded.

- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):
  • Expressed health-related anxiety about possibility of serious illness.  
  • No depressive symptoms or self-harm ideation reported.

- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:
  • Employed; requested sick note for additional days off work.  
  • Lives in the UK (originally from the USA).  
  • No other social determinants discussed.

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:
  • Not recorded (telehealth).

- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated:
  • Not recorded.

- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant:
  • Not examined.

- Ear exam including otoscopy:
  • Not performed.

  • Not performed.

  • Not performed.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected
  • None ordered.

- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated
  • Not ordered.

- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline
  • Not indicated.

- Cervical screening if eligible and due
  • Not recorded.

- Mammography if eligible and not up to date
  • Not recorded.

  • Not recorded.

- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present
  • Not recorded.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification
  • Advised rest, adequate fluid intake, and symptomatic relief with paracetamol.

- Discuss patient health goals and priorities
  • Primary goal: Symptom relief and reassurance regarding seriousness of illness.

- Assess eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA)
  • Not applicable—no chronic disease identified.

- Referral to allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports
  • None at this stage.

- Schedule follow-up and recall appointments as needed
  • Advised to consult GP in person if symptoms worsen, breathlessness increases, or no improvement within 4–5 days.

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral
  • Consider if health anxiety persists.

- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management
  • Not required currently.

- Dental referral if oral health issues identified
  • Not indicated.

- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening
  • Not indicated.

- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected
  • Not indicated.

- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health
  • Not indicated.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):

● Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs, anthropometrics, immunisation review, alcohol intake, comprehensive lifestyle factors, vision/hearing screening, urinalysis, routine chronic disease screening labs.  
● Internal conflicts or contradictions: Patient initially said “No” to shortness of breath then stated “Yes” (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality notes: Telehealth consultation; no physical examination possible; some overlapping dialogue but overall understandable.
